students: Plan a 1-minute scene told with classifiers: setting map, objects placed in space, 4 movements and the order of shots.

title: Classifier Scene Peer Feedback
students: Watch a partner sign their classifier scene and rate clear placement, consistent space and handshape choice with a rubric.

title: Classifiers and Space Review
students: Answer 15 mixed items on classifier types, choosing classifiers, space and indexing, plus one drawing from gloss.

title: Deaf and deaf
students: Read about capital-D Deaf as a cultural identity, answer 5 questions, and sort 6 statements as cultural or medical in focus.

title: Cultural and Medical Views
students: Compare cultural and medical views of deafness in a T-chart from a short reading, with 4 examples for each.

title: Deaf History Timeline
students: Place 10 events on a timeline: 1817 Hartford school, 1864 Gallaudet charter, 1880 Milan, 1988 Deaf President Now, 1990 ADA.

title: Milan 1880: Reading a Resolution
students: Read a translation of the 1880 Milan Congress resolutions on oral education, answer 6 guiding questions, and explain its effects.

title: Deaf President Now: The Four Demands
students: Read the four demands of the 1988 Gallaudet protest, identify the goal behind each, and explain what changed afterward.

title: Access Technology Through Time
students: Sequence 8 access tools (TTY, captions, relay services, video phones, vibrating alarms) and note what each changed.

title: Sign Languages of the World
students: Label 8 sign languages on a world map (ASL, LSF, BSL, JSL, Auslan, LSM) and note that ASL and BSL are unrelated.

title: Community Norms Scenarios
students: Read 8 scenarios (walking through a conversation, interpreting, leaving a group) and choose and explain the culturally right action.

title: De'VIA and Deaf Art
students: Read about the De'VIA art movement and its themes, then describe 3 common symbols and what they express.

title: Community Terms Sort
students: Sort 15 terms (audism, Deaf gain, CODA, residential school, Deaf club) into history, identity and community, and use 5 in sentences.

title: Deaf Guest Visit Planner
students: Plan respectful questions for a Deaf guest or interpreter visit, with seating, sightlines, turn-taking and 6 open questions.

title: Deaf Culture Review
students: Answer 15 mixed items on identity, history, technology, sign languages and community norms.

title: Intermediate ASL Year Review
students: Answer 20 mixed items across grammar, classifiers and Deaf culture, plus one gloss-to-picture task.

title: Intermediate ASL Can-Do Self-Check
students: Rate 12 ACTFL Intermediate can-do statements for ASL, give evidence for 3, and set 2 goals.

title: Deaf Community Organizations
students: Read about the NAD (1880), Deaflympics (1924) and Deaf clubs, answer 5 questions, and explain why such spaces matter.

title: What Makes an ASL Story
students: Read about the features of ASL storytelling (role shift, classifiers, eye gaze, pacing) and answer 6 questions with examples.

title: Role Shift: Turning Shoulders
students: Draw shoulder and eye gaze arrows on figure outlines for 2 characters talking, then mark the shifts in a glossed dialogue.

title: Two Characters, One Signer
students: Gloss a 10-line dialogue between two characters, marking each role shift and the eye gaze direction for each line.

title: Eye Gaze Map
students: Draw a signing space map of a story scene and mark where the narrator looks for 6 people and objects.

title: Elements of a Story Arc
students: Fill a story arc for a fable with exposition, rising action, climax and resolution, and note one ASL device for each.

title: Constructed Action and Dialogue
students: Sort 12 glossed story lines into constructed action, constructed dialogue or narration, then explain 3.

title: Setting the Scene
students: Rewrite 4 bare setting glosses with classifiers placing landmarks in space, sizes and the narrator's viewpoint.

title: Flashbacks and Time Shifts
students: Mark time shifts in 6 story glosses using time signs and body shifts, then add a flashback to one.

title: Pacing Marks
students: Add pause, hold and speed-up marks to a glossed story script and explain how each change builds suspense.

title: Non-Manual Markers in Narrative
students: Add facial grammar and mouth morphemes to 10 lines of a story script and explain the meaning each adds.

title: Character Traits Through Role Shift
students: Plan posture, facial expression, height and signing size for 3 characters and explain how each shows a trait.

title: Midyear Storytelling Review
students: Answer 15 mixed items on role shift, eye gaze, constructed action, scene setting and pacing.

title: ABC Story Planner
students: Plan an ABC story: one sign or classifier for each letter handshape A to Z, with a sketch of the action.

title: Number Story Planner
students: Plan a story using number handshapes 1 to 10 in order, with a sketch and gloss for each step.

title: Handshape Constraint Puzzle
students: Find signs or classifiers for 10 story moments that use only a given handshape, and check them with a partner.

title: Visual Vernacular Basics
students: Read about visual vernacular as a Deaf art form and answer 5 questions on its film-like techniques.

title: Camera Shots in Visual Vernacular
students: Label 6 drawn frames with the camera shot each shows (wide, close-up, slow motion) and gloss how a signer creates it.

title: Visual Vernacular Storyboard
students: Storyboard an 8-frame visual vernacular scene, labeling the shot, classifier and non-manual marker in each frame.

title: ASL Poetry: Handshape Rhyme
students: Read a description of ASL poetry and handshape rhyme, then find the repeated handshapes in 2 glossed poem lines.

title: Veditz 1913: Preservation of the Sign Language
students: Read an English translation of George Veditz's 1913 filmed speech and answer 6 questions on its purpose and audience.

title: Deaf Storytelling Traditions
students: Place 8 events on a timeline of Deaf storytelling, from residential school dorms and Deaf clubs to the first ASL literature films.

title: Story Map for a Fable
students: Map characters, setting, problem, events and moral for an Aesop fable before planning it in ASL.

title: Fable to ASL Translation Plan
students: Translate an Aesop fable into an ASL gloss plan with role shifts, classifier scenes and eye gaze for each part.

title: Picture Strip Retelling
students: Plan an ASL retelling of a wordless 8-panel picture strip, writing the gloss and device for each panel.

title: Adding Depth to a Story
students: Rewrite a flat 8-line story gloss with classifiers, role shift and non-manual markers, then compare the two versions.

title: Gloss Script Frame
students: Write a full gloss script for an original 2-minute story using a frame for opening, setting, events, climax and closing.

title: Mini-Saga Script
students: Write a 50-sign mini-saga in gloss with a twist ending, marking role shifts and pauses.

title: Story for Young Children
students: Plan an ASL story for a kindergarten audience: simple characters, big expressions, repetition and 3 audience participation moments.

title: Folk Tale Adaptation Planner
students: Plan an adaptation of a public domain folk tale into ASL, noting what to keep, change and add for a Deaf audience.

title: Rehearsal Log
students: Over 2 weeks, log 6 rehearsals of a story: time, focus area, a partner's note and one change made.

title: Pacing Chart
students: Time each part of a story across 3 rehearsals, graph the times, and decide which parts to slow or speed.

title: Storyteller Critique Rubric
students: Watch a live story signed by the teacher or a guest and rate role shift, eye gaze, classifiers and pacing with evidence.

title: Peer Story Feedback
students: Watch a partner's story and give two strengths and two next steps tied to specific moments on a rubric.

title: Translation Comparison
students: Compare two glossed ASL renderings of the same English paragraph and judge which keeps meaning and visual clarity better.

title: Storytelling Terms Word Map
students: Build word maps for role shift, constructed action, visual vernacular and handshape rhyme with a definition, sketch and example.

title: Showcase Planner
students: Plan a class storytelling showcase: running order, staging and sightlines, lighting, interpreters and introductions in ASL.

title: Final Storytelling Review
students: Answer 20 mixed items on narrative devices, story genres, visual vernacular and Deaf storytelling history.

title: Performance Self-Assessment
students: Rate your final story on 6 rubric criteria with a reason for each and name one moment you would sign differently.

title: Audience and Purpose Reflection
students: Reflect on how you changed your story for different audiences and what the Deaf storytelling tradition taught you.

title: Advanced ASL Portfolio Reflection
students: Choose 3 pieces of work from the year, rate each against ACTFL Intermediate High descriptors, and explain your growth.
